author: c. d. hulsey
title: Cary highlights ongoing sustainability efforts in Earth Day proclamation
text:
Cary officials marked Earth Day on April 22 by emphasizing the town’s year-round work to protect natural resources and promote sustainability. The Town Council issued a proclamation during its recent meeting, reaffirming Cary’s commitment to environmental stewardship and honoring the Friends of the Page-Walker for their long-standing volunteer service.
The recognition comes as Cary continues its focus on water conservation, energy efficiency, waste reduction, and community engagement. Town leaders said that while Earth Day serves as an annual reminder, their approach is integrated into daily operations, long-term planning, and partnerships with local organizations.
Residents are encouraged to take part in these efforts through actions such as monitoring water usage with tools like Aquastar—allowing them to set alerts and detect leaks—and participating in stormwater programs designed to protect waterways. The town also promotes public education initiatives like Creek Week.
Cary’s status as a Tree City USA community for over four decades reflects its investment in maintaining a healthy tree canopy. Programs such as My Tree, Our Tree distribute native trees directly to residents. Other sustainability measures include transitioning municipal vehicles toward alternative fuels, increasing solar installations at town facilities, and expanding composting and recycling services.
Proper disposal of hazardous household waste remains a priority for keeping pollutants out of local streams and landfills. Officials remind residents that even small habits—like picking up pet waste—can help prevent bacteria from entering lakes and rivers.
To further engage the community this month, Cary invites residents to participate in upcoming events including an Earth Day celebration at Bond Park on Saturday, April 25. The event will coincide with the Spring Daze Arts & Crafts Festival and feature educational activities focused on sustainable practices.
